html:
SMTO-AUT-0015 — The sign-in service didn't accept SMTO's app details

GUID: 83374ac5-7c2d-5205-a691-5bc26f4c5784
Slug: auth-client-authentication-failed
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • The service SMTO signs in to rejected the app ID, secret, key or certificate saved for this connection. This is not about your own password, and SMTO got no access from this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Send the error details to the person who set up this connection, and tell them the service rejected the app details saved in Parameter Store. Signing in again with your own account won't help; only the saved app ID, secret, key or certificate can fix this.
  2. If you manage it: open Parameter Store from the More options (⋯) menu, open the sign-in client entry, select Reveal & edit value, update the secret, key or certificate, and select Save. The service checks these saved values every time SMTO asks for access, so a secret that was changed or reset at the service must be updated here too.
  3. After the details are updated, check whether the task's action, such as sending an email, already happened. Run the task again only if it didn't. SMTO stopped before it got access, but earlier steps of the task may already have run, so checking first avoids doing anything twice.

What success looks like

  • The task gets past the sign-in step without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the client secret, private key or certificate into the conversation or into the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OAuth client authentication failed: the client assertion could not be built from the saved signing key or secret, or the provider returned invalid_client for the configured client authentication method.

What this means

  • Client assertion construction failed or the provider returned invalid_client for the configured authentication method. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Client assertion construction failed or the provider returned invalid_client for the configured authentication method.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the registered client method with its secret, signing key or certificate and the provider's accepted configuration.

How to fix it

  • Open the oauth2_client profile in Parameter Store and confirm client_auth_method matches the provider's registration, then correct client_id and client_secret (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt with at least 32 bytes), private_key_pem and private_key_id (private_key_jwt, RS256), or client_certificate_pem and client_key_pem (tls_client_auth). An invalid_client error means the provider rejected these saved values.
  • Correct the registered client method, secret, signing key or client certificate in Parameter Store.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts the intended client's authentication during the supported exchange.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
